feature_context.prompt: Identify the feature and its existing task plan

steps.prompt: Inspect the existing task plan and current validation evidence for {{ inputs.feature_context }} before implementation. Return a structured outcome envelope with state complete, continue, or blocked; a stable reason_code; repository-relative evidence paths with current SHA-256 digests; remaining_ids for unfinished eligible tasks; resolved_ids; and exactly one of next_step_id or resume_action as required. Mark complete only when no required task remains and relevant validation has passed. Use continue only for specific eligible unfinished tasks and set next_step_id to implement-eligible-work. Use blocked for a specific required operator answer or a concrete prerequisite, failed validation, or unsafe continuation; provide a stable resume_action. This snapshot is the progress baseline; do not invoke implementation or other workflow phases. Routing fields are state-dependent. For `complete`, omit `next_step_id`, `gate_step_id`, and `resume_action`; for `continue`, include only `next_step_id` targeting a declared loop-body step; for `blocked`, include only a stable `resume_action`. Never include a routing field for `complete`. Both `reason_code` and `resume_action` must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$` (lowercase letters and digits joined by single hyphens; never use underscores or spaces).

input.args: On retries, preserve the latest assess-implementation-after-pass exact review findings verbatim for correction only through their existing eligible task IDs; do not invent or reopen tasks. Implement all remaining eligible tasks for {{ inputs.feature_context }} from its existing task plan. Continue until those tasks are complete, a concrete blocker prevents further eligible work, or operator input is required. Preserve completed work and return completed and remaining task IDs, validation results, changed paths, and the exact blocker or question if stopped. Do not re-specify, re-plan, re-task, re-analyze, expand scope, or invoke another FlowKit workflow.

steps.prompt: Inspect the current task checklist, implementation changes, and validation evidence for {{ inputs.feature_context }} after this implementation session. Independently review the changed code for correctness against the selected tasks, regressions evident from the diff, and adequate focused validation. Return exact findings and repository-relative evidence. Keep findings within the existing task plan: use continue only when specific eligible unfinished tasks remain and another speckit.implement session can safely address them. If review finds a material code defect with no remaining eligible task, use blocked with a precise resume_action to update or reopen the task plan and re-invoke; do not silently accept the implementation or invent new tasks. Return a structured outcome envelope with state complete, continue, or blocked; a stable reason_code; repository-relative evidence paths with current SHA-256 digests; remaining_ids for unfinished eligible tasks; resolved_ids for previously unfinished tasks now completed with inspectable evidence; and exactly one of next_step_id or resume_action as required. Mark complete only when the existing task plan is finished, the code review has no material unresolved findings, and relevant validation passed. Use continue only when specific eligible tasks remain, the session completed at least one previously unfinished task, and another speckit.implement session can safely proceed; set next_step_id to implement-eligible-work. Review an attributable implementation delta with changed paths and before/after evidence; if that boundary is unavailable, stop with an untrusted-delta recovery. Return exact review findings as a separate workflow-specific result alongside the strict envelope, retaining stable ID, task_id, artifact_location, violated requirement, observed deficiency, and exact correction. Fresh independent assessment must confirm substantive resolution and retain new blocking findings. With no safe eligible correction route, return blocked with a specific task-recording or reopening resumption action. Preserve the exact unanswered product question and never infer an answer; successful commands cannot discharge findings. A checkbox change, a child saying it is done, or a successful command alone is not completion evidence. Use blocked when a specific operator answer is required or for a concrete prerequisite, failed validation, unavailable command, or unsafe continuation; provide a stable resume_action. Do not re-specify, re-plan, re-task, re-analyze, or invoke another FlowKit workflow. Routing fields are state-dependent. For `complete`, omit `next_step_id`, `gate_step_id`, and `resume_action`; for `continue`, include only `next_step_id` targeting a declared loop-body step; for `blocked`, include only a stable `resume_action`. Never include a routing field for `complete`. Both `reason_code` and `resume_action` must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$` (lowercase letters and digits joined by single hyphens; never use underscores or spaces).

Report the latest evidenced assessment for {{ inputs.feature_context }}. Name completed and remaining task IDs, validation results, changed paths, and the exact blocker or operator question and safe resumption point when work remains. A no-progress or five-pass safety stop is not completion. Stop this workflow here. Converge, roadmap verification, Git integration, and feature acceptance require separate operator action.

workflow.author: pegagio
workflow.description: Repeat the existing implementation skill while eligible tasks remain and progress is evidenced, stopping on completion or a specific bounded blocker.
workflow.name: Implement Eligible Work
